description: The token handoff: the Control UI URL with `#token=<token>` merged into its fragment. `core/test/fixtures.test.js` asserts the JS reproduces every case and `mobile/ChelaTests/GatewayURLParityTests.swift` asserts the Swift port does, so a client that hands a credential over hands over the same address as the other one.
why: The Control UI accepts a token on the URL fragment: it reads it during boot, stores it for that gateway, and strips it from the address bar. The fragment is the documented preference over `?token=`, because a fragment never reaches an HTTP request log or a Referer header. This is what lets a client supply the credential instead of asking someone to paste one into a page, and because it is reapplied on every connect it also self-heals a stale stored token.

Pure URL construction with no platform in it, which is why it can be shared at all. The two behaviours worth pinning are here because a port is most likely to get them wrong: an existing fragment is PRESERVED and only the `token` key is set, and a URL that will not parse is handed back untouched rather than thrown, because the caller's next move is to load it and let the real navigation fail with a real error rather than crash on a typo in Settings.
A falsy token leaves the address exactly as it was, INCLUDING when it already carries a fragment. This is the case a port gets wrong by treating an empty token as `set the key to the empty string`.

cases.name: no token leaves the address alone
an empty token is no token
an address with no fragment gains one
an existing fragment is kept and the token is added
a token already in the fragment is replaced rather than duplicated
a port and a path survive
a token that needs encoding is encoded
an address that will not parse is handed back untouched
